## What is GPT-6.1 Terra?

GPT-6.1 Terra is OpenAI's fast, lower-cost GPT-6.1 model, built for computer use, visual reasoning, and clear writing at half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI's launch post calls it "a significant step up" from GPT-5.6 Terra, the version it released in July.

It sits between Luna and Sol in the GPT-6 lineup. As OpenAI's Ted Sanders put it on Hacker News, the order is "Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra," and if you're "very price sensitive," pick Terra or Luna.

The specs that matter, from OpenAI's model page: [...] TL;DR:

 What it is: OpenAI's fast, lower-cost GPT-6.1 model for computer use, visual reasoning, and writing.
 Released: October 26, 2026.
 API price: $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 cached, and $5 output, which is half of GPT-6.1 Sol's rates.
 Where to use it: ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu, plus the API (gpt-6.1-terra), GitHub Copilot, and Amazon Bedrock. It isn't in regular ChatGPT chat.
 Biggest caveat: It's best at max effort, but that's also where it uses the most tokens, so your bill ends up closer to Sol's than you'd expect.

## What is GPT-6.1 Terra? [...] ### What is GPT-6.1 Terra?

GPT-6.1 Terra is OpenAI's fast, lower-cost GPT-6.1 model for computer use, visual reasoning, and writing, released on October 26, 2026. It sits between GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol in OpenAI's lineup and costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens on the API.

### Is GPT-6.1 Terra good?

Yes, GPT-6.1 Terra is a strong mid-priced model, especially for computer use and writing. It scores 51 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index at max effort, four points behind GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on its Agents' Last Exam computer-use test at medium effort. The catch is that its scores drop fast at lower effort settings.

results.title: GPT-6.1 Terra vs Soul vs Luna: Which One Should You Use? | MindStudio
results.content:
GPT-6.1 Terra is the middle tier of OpenAI’s three-model GPT-6.1 family, sitting between the lightweight Luna and the flagship Soul. OpenAI positions Terra as a faster, cheaper alternative to Soul aimed at computer-use tasks, roughly half the cost of Soul with quicker response times. The catch is that it also gives up a meaningful chunk of reasoning quality compared to Soul, while still costing more than Luna. That middle-of-the-road positioning is the whole story with Terra: it’s not the cheap option and it’s not the smart option, it’s the option in between.

## TL;DR [...] GPT-6.1 Terra costs about half of what Soul costs and runs faster, but testers found it noticeably less capable on complex tasks like 3D generation and agentic reasoning.
 GPT-6.1 Luna is the budget pick, with input costs roughly ten times cheaper than Terra and output costs around ten times cheaper too, making it the better deal for simple, high-volume tasks.
 GPT-6.1 Soul remains the model worth paying for when a task needs real horsepower, since it produced dramatically better results than Terra in side-by-side 3D modeling tests.
 On Agent’s Last Exam, Terra reportedly beats GPT-5.6, but in hands-on use across real tasks it often performed closer to Luna than to Soul.

results.content:
GPT-6 Astra — the flagship, still OpenAI's strongest for the hardest computer-use and engineering work, at premium prices.
 GPT-6.1 Sol — the model for complex, multistep coding and agentic work where depth matters more than cost.
 GPT-6.1 Terra — the fast, cheap workhorse for high-volume computer use: forms, invoices, proposals, technical drawings, and video edits, where price-per-task and speed win.

A practical pattern for agent builders: route routine, well-defined computer-use steps to Terra, and escalate only the hardest coding subtasks to Sol or Astra. With Terra priced at half of Sol, that kind of model routing is a real cost lever.
